applies_why: This is a judge-seat link collision at Matthew 1:16, and the judge resolves it by single-verse ambiguity rather than by weighing the parties' chains by footing.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: the phrase "never verse by verse": (1) the judge may not decide the collision by finding one pressed verse underdetermined; (2) the judge may note a single verse's ambiguity as part of chain-footing analysis.
why: The judge labels Matthew 1:16 underdetermined because the verse's own wording admits both readings, which is verse-by-verse analysis and not the required chain-against-chain weighing by footing.
